options.name: Notice
options.description: Perform this check AFTER waterproofing is dry, but BEFORE tiling starts.

nodes.name: Membrane Coverage Overview (Walls & Floor)
nodes.description: Check if the waterproofing membrane (a rubbery paint) covers the entire floor and required wall areas. The coating should look thick and consistent, not see-through. Tip: Take a wide-angle photo from the doorway showing the whole floor and walls.

nodes.name: Shower Zone Height Check
nodes.description: Verify the waterproofing on the shower walls goes high enough. It should typically reach a height of at least 1.8m (approx. 6ft) or up to the ceiling rose. Tip: Stand in the shower area and check if the "paint" goes up above your head level.

nodes.name: Corners & Bond Breaker Check
nodes.description: Inspect the bottom corners where the wall meets the floor, and the vertical corners inside the shower. These areas should look reinforced with a tape or thick sealant (Bond Breaker) under the membrane, not just simple paint. Tip: The corner should look "curved" or "taped", not a sharp 90-degree crack. This prevents the membrane from tearing when the house moves.

nodes.name: Penetrations & Drain Sealing
nodes.description: Check around the water pipes (taps/mixer) and the floor drain (waste). The membrane must tightly seal around these holes with no gaps. Tip: Look closely at the tap mixer coming out of the wall. There should be no gap between the pipe and the waterproofing.
